caption: A real world atlas based on Natural Earth geography. Destination markers are approximate; close-together stops are easier to find in the place index. Personal chapters are distinguished from imagined journeys.

places.name: Kerala
places.intro: The air smells like rain and something frying. Probably a good sign.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of leaves moving after rain.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Kerala has a suspicious talent for turning a rainy afternoon into a core memory. The coconut trees are doing their best impression of a welcoming committee, and nobody has asked you to check your emails.

places.name: Kuwait
places.intro: For an ordinary Kuwait evening that deserves to be remembered.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of the evening sky from your window.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, the Kuwait Towers are standing very tall for a city that already has enough confidence. If the skyline could send a voice note, it would probably say: 'The sunsets here are surprisingly good. Bring snacks.'

places.name: Bengaluru
places.intro: The familiar chaos, with a very good snack somewhere nearby.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of a street corner with its own rhythm.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Bengaluru has a parliament building fit for royalty and traffic that insists everyone deserves a longer podcast. Keep the Vidhana Soudha photo; blur the part where you negotiated with an auto driver.

places.name: Munnar
places.intro: Clouds that behave like they own the tea estates.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of cloud drifting across the hills.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, the tea hills have arranged themselves in perfect lines, apparently without a single calendar invite. The clouds are refusing to leave the meeting, and for once that feels completely fine.

places.name: Manali
places.intro: A winding road. An excuse for another playlist.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of a mountain road or rolling mist.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Manali ordered extra mountains and forgot to mention the cold. Your sweater gets the starring role, the hot chai wins Best Supporting Actor, and the snow refuses to follow the itinerary.

places.name: Ladakh
places.intro: An enormous sky. A very small list of worries.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of a wide sky and changing light.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, the mountains here look as though someone crumpled the planet and forgot to smooth it out. Even your thoughts would need an extra layer and a little more breathing room.

places.name: Nepal
places.intro: A road bends around the mountain and makes you look up again. One day, perhaps, with a camera in your hand.
places.prompt: Film 10 seconds of clouds drifting across a mountain view.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Nepal has mountains so tall they make everyday drama seem delightfully pocket-sized. Take one look at the Himalayas, then explain to your camera why it cannot possibly fit all of this into one frame.

places.name: Alleppey
places.intro: Where a houseboat is the most convincing argument for doing nothing at all.
places.translation: Let's stay here a little longer.
places.prompt: Film the water moving past a houseboat while everybody else argues over the best snack.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Alleppey has a genius business model: put a roof on a boat and call doing absolutely nothing an itinerary. The backwaters do the sightseeing; you are officially appointed Chief Snack Inspector.

places.name: Mysore
places.intro: A palace with more fairy lights than a wedding planner's wildest spreadsheet.
places.prompt: Film the palace at twilight and count how long it takes to say 'wow' without saying 'wow'.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Mysore Palace lights up like it has an extremely ambitious electricity bill. Somewhere inside, even the chandeliers are probably saying, 'We do clean up rather nicely.'

places.name: Jaipur
places.intro: A pink city that makes an ordinary building feel underdressed.
places.prompt: Find a perfectly framed window, then narrate why pink is a perfectly sensible citywide decision.
places.postcardBack: Dear Maha, Jaipur decided that one pink wall was simply not enough and turned the whole city into a mood board. Please ask the Hawa Mahal how it keeps 953 windows clean; this is urgent research.
